title: Who are Dakar's neighbours?
hook: Senegal faces Europe to the north and Brazil across the ocean. Which is really closer?

knows: that Africa and South America face each other across the Atlantic
roughly where Paris, Rome and Senegal are
doesNotKnow: how close West Africa is to Brazil compared with Europe
a map that keeps true distance from one point

misconception: West Africa is far from Brazil and close to Europe.
objective: The learner can explain that from Dakar, Natal in Brazil (about 3,000 km) is nearer than Paris or Rome (over 4,000 km), and that an azimuthal equidistant map keeps true distances from its centre only.

claims.text: Natal, Brazil is about 3,000 km from Dakar.
claims.source: d3-geo geoDistance x 6,371.0088 km from Dakar (14.7167°N, 17.4677°W) to Natal (5.79°S, 35.2°W) = 3,003.6 km (shown to the nearest 10 km). Sphere model. Coordinates from the brief, which cites a gazetteer; the builder did not check them online. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Node haversine R=6371.0088: Dakar (14.7167N,17.4677W; Wikipedia 14 44N 17 28W) to Natal (5.79S,35.2W) = 3,004 km. Coordinates match gazetteer values (Natal 5 47S 35 12W).

claims.text: Rome is about 4,170 km and Paris about 4,210 km from Dakar.
claims.source: Same method: Rome (41.9028°N, 12.4964°E) 4,170.3 km; Paris (48.8566°N, 2.3522°E) 4,205.1 km. City coordinates from memory, not checked online. Shown in the reveal only if the learner's ring reached past both; otherwise the reveal quotes the learner's widest ring. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Node: Rome 4,170 km, Paris 4,205 km (shown 4,210). Paris 48.8566N 2.3522E and Rome 41.9028N 12.4964E are the standard coordinates. The brief's '4,210' for Paris is the stage's rounding of 4,205.1.

claims.text: An azimuthal equidistant map keeps true distance from its centre only; distances between other pairs are stretched.
claims.source: Snyder (1987), Map Projections: A Working Manual, USGS PP 1395, ch. 25. From memory, not checked online. d3-geo geoAzimuthalEquidistant centred on Dakar. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Azimuthal equidistant: distances true from the centre only (Snyder, Map Projections - A Working Manual, USGS PP 1395, ch. 25).

claims.text: Of Paris, Rome and Natal, Natal is the nearest to Dakar.
claims.source: Follows from c1 and c2. The lesson does not claim Natal is the nearest city to Dakar overall (Lisbon, 2,791 km, is nearer) or the nearest in Brazil. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): 3,004 km (Natal) < 4,170 (Rome) < 4,205 (Paris); at ring slider stops Natal is inside from 3,500 km (ring 3,000 sits 4 km short of Natal) and neither European city until 4,500 km.

claims.text: Senegal faces Europe to the north and Brazil across the ocean.
claims.source: Hook. Geographic description: Europe lies to the north-north-east of Senegal, Brazil to the south-west across the Atlantic (visible on the stage map). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Hook text. Initial bearing Dakar to Paris is about north-north-east and to Natal about south-west (node check below); consistent with the stage map.

recall.question: On a map centred on one city, you draw a circle round it. When is that circle a true distance ring?
options: On an azimuthal equidistant map centred on that city
recall.why: An azimuthal equidistant map keeps true distance from its centre in every direction, so rings round the centre are real circles on the ground.
